claims.text: Partial electrochemical dealloying of a noble-metal-rich precursor alloy can produce a three-dimensional nanoporous high-entropy alloy framework.
Electrochemical dealloying selectively removes less noble elements from the precursor.
Selective removal leaves an interconnected noble-metal network with high surface area.
The proposed precursor is a homogeneous alloy containing both noble and less noble metals.
A suitable aqueous electrolyte and controlled electrochemical potential can preferentially dissolve the less noble components.
Moderate temperature and carefully monitored potential permit preferential etching of the more reactive elements.
Selective dissolution drives formation of a nanoscale bicontinuous network in the remaining noble-metal framework.
Electrochemical oxidation of the less noble metals creates a transient protective passivation layer on the noble metals.
The proposed passivation layer permits selective removal of the more reactive elements.
Selective removal leaves a porous, high-entropy nanostructure.
The resulting three-dimensional nanoframework has a high surface-to-volume ratio.
The resulting three-dimensional nanoframework has improved catalytic properties.
Before dealloying, the precursor alloy has minimal surface porosity.
The undealloyed precursor has lower catalytic performance than the proposed dealloyed material.
The approach is most effective when constituent metals have sufficiently different electrochemical potentials to enable selective dissolution.
Unconfirmed relative etch rates and nonuniform constituent distributions could impair pore-size uniformity and final catalytic performance.
